articles.summary: A 61-year-old man has retrained as a flight attendant after decades in the travel industry, finding that his skills are well-suited to the role.
articles.content: Richard Woulfe marked his 60th birthday with a sense of restlessness and discontent with his life's trajectory so far. He had been in the travel industry for decades, but felt an insatiable urge to pursue something new. Woulfe's dissatisfaction led him to retrain as a flight attendant at the age of 61, embarking on a third chapter in his life. He is now employed by a major US airline and has found that his skills as a flight attendant are well-suited to his personality. He believes that qualities commonly associated with Gen X individuals, such as flexibility and a willingness to listen, have been invaluable assets in his new role. Woulfe's decision to change careers was motivated by a desire for challenge and personal growth. The pandemic had a significant impact on Woulfe's business, causing his main markets to shut down due to travel restrictions imposed by countries like Thailand. As a result, he was forced to return to Chicago and take some time off, where he spent quality time with his parents. Woulfe's father was struggling with health issues at the age of 90, and Woulfe wanted to be there for him as much as possible during this challenging period. This experience likely had a profound impact on Woulfe, who would soon find himself re-evaluating his life and career choices. After celebrating his 60th birthday in March 2023, Woulfe's mother noticed that he seemed restless and asked if everything was okay. Woulfe reassured her that he wasn't depressed but rather feeling unfulfilled, which sparked a conversation about his future plans. Woulfe reached out to a friend who had been working as a flight attendant since 2018 for advice on how to get back into the workforce. His friend's encouragement was timely, and Woulfe began to consider making a career change that would bring him new challenges and opportunities for personal growth. As Woulfe reflected on his life, he realized he wasn't ready to retire at 60. He considered making a change that would bring new challenges and opportunities for growth. The transport industry had long fascinated him, dating back to his childhood when he was more interested in the journey than the destination. Woulfe's friend, who had been working as a flight attendant since 2018, offered valuable advice on this potential career path. He encouraged Woulfe to leverage his experience in travel and hospitality for a new role. With that encouragement, Woulfe began exploring the possibility of becoming a flight attendant himself. He discovered that several major US airlines were hiring thousands of flight attendants at the time. This sparked his interest further, and he started applying to various carriers. Although there was some back-and-forth due to personal circumstances, Woulfe eventually secured an interview within 72 hours. As he prepared for this new career, Woulfe noticed a trend among his peers - many Gen-X individuals were willing to acquire new skills and pursue non-traditional careers at an older age. He found this particularly inspiring, especially when he encountered candidates in their 60s and 70s who were also vying for the role of flight attendant. As Richard Woulfe approached his 60th birthday, he realized that retirement wasn't for him. Instead of slowing down, he decided to acquire new skills and stay in the job market. Woulfe's decision paid off as he found a fulfilling career as a flight attendant, where his life experience and ability to listen came into play. His mantra is simple: "I hear you," whenever a passenger raises an issue, showing that people want to feel heard. This approach has been key to his success in this role. The last two years have been amazing for Woulfe as he's had the opportunity to travel to various destinations, from international cities like San José, Costa Rica and Vancouver, to small domestic places like Colombia, South Carolina. His message to anyone considering a lifestyle pivot is clear: if something is calling you, it's worth taking a risk. articles.title: Nasdaq 100 Index Declines Amid Concerns Over Valuing AI Firms
articles.summary: Billionaire investor Howard Marks has expressed doubts over traditional valuation methods for predicting future earnings of AI companies like Anthropic.
articles.content: Billionaire investor Howard Marks has pinpointed a major challenge in valuing AI companies like Anthropic. In an interview on "Bloomberg: The China Show" on Monday, Marks acknowledged that traditional valuation methods often fail when it comes to predicting the future earnings of AI firms. Value investors typically try to estimate a company's earnings five years from now to determine if its current stock price is attractive. However, Marks doubts that this approach can be effectively applied to many AI companies. Anthropic, the developer of the popular chatbot Claude, has filed to go public in what could become one of the largest initial public offerings (IPOs) on record. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index experienced a significant decline last week, plummeting by approximately 1,400 points or nearly 5% over Thursday and Friday. Despite this drop, the index remains in positive territory for the year, having risen around 13% so far. However, the broader market's performance has been even more impressive, with the Nasdaq 100 soaring by a substantial 160% since the end of 2022. The index has effectively doubled its value over this period, rising from under 11,000 points to just below 28,400 points. Investors are being cautioned against making impulsive decisions in response to short-term market fluctuations, with billionaire Howard Marks emphasizing that there is no reward for "hyperactivity" in the investment business. This approach is in line with the long-term investing philosophy championed by Warren Buffett, who has built a reputation for holding onto stakes in companies like Coca-Cola and American Express since acquiring them in the mid-1990s. Valuing AI companies has proven to be a challenging task due to market trends favoring speculative investments over traditional value-based approaches. Investors like Michael Burry have sounded alarms about potential bubbles in the AI sector, citing aggressive accounting practices, hidden debts, and circular deals as warning signs that are often overlooked by enthusiastic investors. articles.title: Rainbow Rowell Publishes Novel Under Pseudonym in 2022
articles.summary: The novel Corinne tells a poignant tale of love and identity centered around a young woman defying her family's fundamentalist upbringing.
articles.content: A highly anticipated novel has been making waves in the literary world since its publication in 2022: Corinne. At its core is a poignant tale of love and identity, centered around Corinne, a young woman who defies her family's fundamentalist upbringing to pursue a path that feels authentic. However, what sets this story apart from others by acclaimed author Rainbow Rowell is the personal connection she has to it. While not a direct account of her life, the novel contains striking parallels to her own experiences. This intimate familiarity made publishing Corinne under a pseudonym a necessity for her in 2022. The secrecy surrounding the book's authorship was lifted when its reissue was announced for July 2027, with Rowell's name finally on the cover. The decision to reveal her identity and share this work with readers marks a significant shift for the celebrated author of Cherry Baby and Eleanor Park. The author's success had reached a peak around that time, having published three consecutive No. 1 bestsellers in rapid succession. This surge in popularity provided an opportune moment to consider releasing new work, but it was not the primary factor driving the decision. The author had already completed the first draft of the novel at a remarkable pace, pouring their thoughts and emotions into the story. The book's central theme revolved around a young woman who is expelled from her strict Christian church as a teenager and subsequently cut off by her family due to her perceived transgressions. As the author of the novel, Corinne was initially hesitant to share details about her pseudonym, Rebecca Morrow. The decision to use a pen name had been made in part because the book's themes of shame and secrecy seemed at odds with publicly promoting it. Corinne's editor and she struggled over how much information to release about Rebecca Morrow, weighing the benefits against the potential risks. The author behind the pseudonym Rebecca Morrow had deliberately crafted a book that sounded like her own unique voice, despite attempting to break free from familiar writing habits. This strategy was intended to make readers guess who the actual author was, but it didn't quite work out as planned. Some readers did manage to identify the author, though their guesses were likely incorrect due to the book's distinctive style. The author had expected this outcome and wasn't bothered by it, choosing not to reveal their identity despite the speculation. The author's favorite book is Corinne, which features two characters that hold a special place in their heart. These characters are particularly notable because they embody many of the author's own flaws and burdens, making them feel incredibly relatable and authentic. The author's emotional connection to their work is palpable in every line. They've poured their heart and soul into creating relatable characters that feel authentic, almost as if they're people rather than fictional creations. This emotional investment has a profound effect on readers, making them invested in the characters' journeys. The author's desire for forgiveness and redemption in their characters resonates deeply with readers. It's a universal human experience to want to forgive others, and seeing this played out through the characters makes it all the more relatable. The author's own flaws and burdens are reflected in these characters, making them feel incredibly real and authentic. The author's decision to revise the book for its new edition is also significant. They've taken the opportunity to delve deeper into certain themes, such as the church's role in the story, and sharpened their focus on specific characters. The revised version is a little longer than the original, but the author believes it's also a little better, offering readers a richer and more nuanced experience. The author behind the pseudonym Rebecca Morrow has been keeping their personal and professional lives separate, a skill they attribute to their therapist describing them as adept at compartmentalizing. This ability allows them to keep certain aspects of themselves hidden from others, but it also means that some parts of their life have felt unfinished or unexplored. The author believes this skill is useful in many situations, but acknowledges that it can be limiting when trying to express oneself fully. As the years passed, the author felt a growing need to reconnect with the creative work they had initially started under the pseudonym Rebecca Morrow. They eventually decided to revisit and revise the book, which has resulted in a revised version that is slightly longer than the original but offers readers a more nuanced experience. The author's decision to bring their characters home is a significant step towards integrating different aspects of themselves, allowing for a more authentic expression of their creativity.
